trust_decision.summary: A server-supplied DataRow field count must be proven equal to the statement's column count before a Row or SimpleQueryRow is exposed, so a short row is rejected as a parse error instead of indexing past the field list and panicking; the decision is placed in the two row constructors in tokio-postgres/src/row.rs.

landing_point.why: The panic is `self.ranges[idx]` (row.rs:194) where idx comes from the column list (row.rs:171-176); the first place an engineer looks for a DataRow/column mismatch is the typed Row constructor that builds both the column list and the field ranges.

fix_sites.entry_point: Client::query / query_one / query_opt / query_raw / query_typed* / query_portal (and postgres::Client, postgres::Transaction, postgres::RowIter) -> RowStream (query.rs:344-353) -> Row::new; then Row::get (row.rs:146) or Row::try_get (row.rs:158)
fix_sites.module_kind: core protocol row type (extended query protocol)

fix_sites.entry_point: Client::simple_query / Client::simple_query_raw (and postgres::Client::simple_query) -> SimpleQueryStream (simple_query.rs:104-109) -> SimpleQueryRow::new; then SimpleQueryRow::get (row.rs:250) or try_get (row.rs:261)
fix_sites.module_kind: simple-query stream row type (text rows, separate public API)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: simple_query is a convenience path that returns text rows (SimpleQueryMessage::Row with Option<&str>), so a solver can call its row type a separate feature and apply the advisory's DataRow panic only to the typed Row path.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A DataRow whose field count matches the columns must still be accepted (fix.diff:116-120), including a matching row with NULL fields; and in a multi-statement simple query the column list legitimately changes between statements (simple_query.rs:101 replaces `*this.columns` on every RowDescription), so a fix that pins the first column count or rejects a row after a RowDescription change breaks legitimate use.

O6_input_shapes: field count smaller than the column count (the reported panic shape, rejected)
field count larger than the column count (also rejected because the check uses != and not <, fix.diff:31)
matching field count containing NULL entries (null is a -1 length, backend.rs:579-580; same count applies and must stay accepted)

O7_producer.where: tokio-postgres/src/prepare.rs:93-107 builds the Statement column schema from RowDescription (same job at tokio-postgres/src/query.rs:98-116 and tokio-postgres/src/simple_query.rs:93-100); the DataRow field count is parsed independently from another message in postgres-protocol/src/message/backend.rs:164-168. The check reads the stored schema through Statement::columns (tokio-postgres/src/statement.rs:72-74) and never re-parses RowDescription.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the same declared-count-vs-expected-columns check for COPY BINARY rows (compared against user-supplied types) before ranges are indexed at binary_copy.rs:250
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the maintainers already wrote exactly this guard on that path, so a third row-shaped path would copy the idiom; it is also the shape a planted sibling should imitate because its count source (user types) differs from Row's (Statement columns)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a statement-less row path: on Message::NoData query_typed hands RowStream a Statement::unnamed(vec![], vec![]) while still consuming whatever DataRows arrive
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: a maintainer adding a describe-then-execute shortcut would reuse this branch, and then the column list is empty while the server still controls the field count - the same split identity with no check

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a public DataRowBody::field_count() or row-building helper in the lower-level crate that pairs a field list with a caller-supplied column list
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: DataRowBody and its ranges() are already public and used outside tokio-postgres, so a helper there is plausible; a fix placed at that layer cannot see the column count and must be duplicated in every consumer

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the generated composite FromSql field-count check (wire count vs compile-time field list)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the derive already implements this exact mechanism for composite values in another package, so a row-mapping derive or a second decoded type is a realistic place for a maintainer to write it again - possibly with <= instead of != or without the check

O9_family: out-of-bounds read / index-out-of-bounds panic on a protocol row whose backing field list is shorter than its column list (CWE-125)

O10_build.toolchain: cargo workspace, edition 2024, rust-version 1.85 (tokio-postgres/Cargo.toml:12); CI pins 1.85.0 (.github/workflows/ci.yml:88)
services: PostgreSQL server for the crate's integration tests (docker compose up -d at .github/workflows/ci.yml:87; tests dial 127.0.0.1:5433 at tokio-postgres/tests/test/main.rs:57) - not needed by the fix's own unit test
O10_build.project_tests: No test at the pinned commit feeds a malformed DataRow (grep over tokio-postgres/tests finds none); tokio-postgres/tests/test/main.rs is a live-database suite. tokio-postgres/Cargo.toml:15 sets [lib] test = false, so the #[cfg(test)] module the fix adds to row.rs (fix.diff:70-121) is not run by cargo test; exercising the behaviour needs an in-crate test that is currently disabled or a mock server on a loopback socket driving a real client.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Bounds-check the accessor instead of the constructor: make Row::col_buffer (row.rs:194) use self.ranges.get(idx) and return an error, which stops the panic the report shows but leaves Row::len()/columns() inconsistent and never touches SimpleQueryRow::get_inner (row.rs:277) where the same ranges[idx] panics.

out_of_scope_notes: No issue outside this advisory was noticed or pursued; the only adjacent count check found (postgres-derive/src/fromsql.rs:204-208) is already guarded and unrelated to this panic.
